note: Webform Validation adds three cross-element rules to Webform elements: equal values (#equal__enabled + #equal__components), compare two values (#compare__enabled + #compare__component + #compare__operator one of > >= < <= + #compare__custom_error), and some of several (#some_of_several__enabled + #some_of_several__components + #some_of_several__completed + #some_of_several__final_validation). No admin page/config schema/permissions/Drush/plugin types/configure route. Rules are stored as #-prefixed element properties inside a webform.webform.<id> config entity's elements YAML; runtime validation is WebformValidateConstraint::validate appended to the submission form #validate. Supported types: ALLOWED_TYPES (date, datetime, email, hidden, number, select, tel, textarea, textfield, webform_document_file, webform_entity_checkboxes, webform_signature, webform_time); compare limited to ALLOWED_TYPES_COMPARE (date, datetime, number, webform_time). Medium/hard cases are grounded in real webform element config: introspection reads a configured rule; execution adds an equal or compare rule to a webform element.

evals.prompt: What cross-field validation rules does the Drupal webform_validation module add to Webform, and where in the UI do you configure them?
evals.expected_output: Three rules configured per element in the 'Form extra validation' fieldset when editing a webform element: Equal values (components must match), Compare two values (>, >=, <, <=), and Some of several (require N of a group of components).

evals.prompt: Using the Drupal webform_validation module, how do I make a 'Confirm email' webform element require the same value as the 'Email' element? Which element properties store this and where are they saved?
evals.expected_output: Enable the 'Equal values' rule on the Confirm email element and select the Email element. This stores #equal__enabled: 1 and #equal__components (a map of element keys) on that element inside the webform config entity's elements YAML.

evals.prompt: In the Drupal webform_validation module, which element types can use the 'Compare two values' rule, and what operators are available?
evals.expected_output: Compare only applies to types in ALLOWED_TYPES_COMPARE: date, datetime, number, webform_time. Operators are >, >=, <, <= (set via #compare__operator), with an optional #compare__custom_error message.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a webform with machine id wfv_known. One of its elements has a webform_validation cross-field rule configured. Inspect the live webform configuration and state which element has a rule, which rule it is, and which element it validates against.
evals.expected_output: The wfv_confirm element has an 'Equal values' rule: #equal__enabled: 1 with #equal__components mapping wfv_email, so wfv_confirm must equal wfv_email.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the webform wfv_compare has a webform_validation 'Compare two values' rule on one of its number elements. Inspect the live configuration and state which comparison operator is configured and against which element.
evals.expected_output: The wfv_max element has #compare__enabled: 1, #compare__component: wfv_min and #compare__operator: '>', so wfv_min must be greater than wfv_max per the module's compare semantics.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the webform wfv_task has two email elements, wfv_email and wfv_confirm, with no validation. Using the webform_validation module, configure the wfv_confirm element so it must hold the same value as wfv_email, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: On webform wfv_task the wfv_confirm element carries #equal__enabled: 1 and #equal__components including wfv_email (set via the element's 'Form extra validation' > Equal values, or by editing the webform elements config).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the webform wfv_range has two number elements, wfv_start and wfv_end, with no validation. Using the webform_validation module, add a 'Compare two values' rule to the wfv_end element that compares it against wfv_start using the greater-than '>' operator, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: On webform wfv_range the wfv_end element carries #compare__enabled: 1, #compare__component: wfv_start and #compare__operator: '>' (set via the element's 'Form extra validation' > Compare, or by editing the webform elements config). Note the module's compare semantics: with '>' the compared-with element wfv_start must be greater than wfv_end.
